messages.author: daf017f67eba24e8
messages.subject: lines across world map
parts:
Hi-

(I havent been able to find an answer in the archives but surely
someone has dealt with this...)

When I use "maps" and then plot the world country outlines, I get
horizontal lines across the plot. Needless to say, these are annoying
and undesired.

require(maps)
world <- data.frame(map("world", plot=FALSE)[c("x","y")])
ggplot( world, aes(x=x,y=y)) + geom_path( ) +coord_map()

looking at a summary of world, one is tempted to think that

world$x=( (world$x+180) %% 360) -180

would solve the problem, but it does not.

Thanks in advance.

James

messages.author: 99a1cfc66539313c
messages.subject: Re: lines across world map
parts:
James

One workaround is to add a fairly arbitratry, large positive number to
the x-values. For example, use 180 or 360.

library(ggplot2)

This will result in a map without horizontal lines, *but* will clearly
only be useful if it is not important to have the longitude labelled.

Andrie
